text:
Debt-ridden broadcaster JTBC said Monday it has terminated its contract with the International Olympic Committee to air the Olympics in Korea.
"With the contract termination, JTBC has eliminated financial uncertainties and established a more stable foundation for management," the company said, adding the decision was made as it was difficult to maintain its Olympic broadcast business.
The financial details of the decision will be included in the company's third-quarter regulatory filing, the company said.
JTBC had secured the broadcast rights for the Winter and Summer Olympics from 2026-2032 and for the World Cup from 2026-2030.
In August, a Seoul court approved the broadcaster's request to begin rehabilitation proceedings, allowing the company to restructure its debts under court supervision.
Earlier this month, JTBC put up an official notice for its sale, with the aim to select a preferred bidder in January.
